summary.prose: S001 keeps the existing single Milkdown pane and 1 MiB Markdown file contract, but removes full-document validation from typing. Edits render immediately and stage recoverable drafts; a 300 ms typing gap validates only the latest generation in background execution before native application. Explicit Save/Send and native lifecycle actions flush their captured generation, while stale work cannot overwrite newer typing.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: The daemon-owned private repository-keyed index remains authoritative for link resolution, backlinks and the title/preview list read-model. Client-side scratchpad editing now uses Milkdown + Crepe inside a VS Code CustomTextEditorProvider on the existing .md TextDocument, replacing the host's built-in vscode.markdown.editor. Insrc owns its selection toolbar and lock state without a native-editor extension API dependency. [[c40]] [[c41]] [[c42]]

ownedContracts.name: ScratchpadRef
ownedContracts.purpose: The one cross-cutting note-identity primitive every link-, lifecycle-, and citation-facing story needs: a stable reference to a scratchpad that survives rename/move/archive/restore. Owned at s1 (the Epic's root) because s2 — which depends only on s1, not on s7 where identity is semantically 'about' — also needs it for the k2 tie-break.

boundary.internal: Milkdown + Crepe hosted in one VS Code CustomTextEditorProvider pane is private to s1. It owns rendering/editing, per-pane lock/pencil controls, explicit selection Send popup, versioned transaction/document synchronization, local asset packaging and TextDocument lifecycle integration. It preserves the .md file and sc1 identity, replaces the old textarea/save protocol atomically and retains browse/new/delete/send/list-refresh behavior. Locked mode keeps selection and Send available; a custom tooltip may be needed because default formatting toolbars can hide when read-only. No s8 attachments, s7 metadata persistence, backlinks or search ranking are implemented here.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The chat-menu cap-10 rendering, the list panel's cap-20/3-line-preview/delete UI, and the relevance-ranking algorithm itself (title-first, tie-break via sc1's stableId) are private to s2; sc3 exposes only the read-model shape (title/preview/mtime), not the ranking logic.

Find-in-note's match highlighting, wraparound navigation, and collapsed-section reveal operate entirely on the open editor's live text buffer — no cross-story data or contract is produced or consumed.

The entry-boundary/timestamp Markdown convention, day-grouping, and the Undated bucket are private to how one note's content renders; no story downstream of s4 in the Epic's dependency graph consumes dated-entry structure, so it is not exposed as a shared contract.

The link-target picker UI and the qualified-target Markdown syntax (percent-encoded target segments, versioned, per the HLD's resolved open question) are private to s5; sc2 exposes only the resolved-reference and backlink-query shape s6 consumes, not the authoring UI or syntax.
The backlink view's grouping-by-source-note rendering, on the pad and on file/symbol surfaces, is private UI; no story is downstream of s6 in the Epic's graph, so it exposes no further contract.

The archive/restore state machine, the permanent-delete confirmation flow, and the decision of where stable ID/repo-association/archive-state are actually persisted are private to s7; it extends sc1's bare ScratchpadRef with lifecycle state but does not re-expose that lifecycle representation as a further contract, since s8/s9/s10 only need sc1's identity.

The attach-to-turn picker UI, the removable-preview rendering, and revision-pinning for a queued turn are private to s8; it consumes sc1 to cite the note and exposes no further contract, since only s9 depends on s8 and s9's own need (provenance link) is satisfied by sc1 directly.
The promote-to-draft action's brainstorm/ISSUE routing and idempotent-retry handling are private to s9; no story is downstream of s9 in the Epic's graph.
The tag-filter UI and starter-template catalog are private to s10; it extends sc3's list read-model with the tags field but no story is downstream of s10 in the Epic's graph.

nonFunctional.performance: The list panel (s2) must not re-parse every on-disk pad file per render; sc3's read-model is served from the daemon's index instead. Backlink-query latency targets and the note-size cap for sc2's new daemon IPC are explicitly an open PRD decision (DEF §8) to resolve before s2/s5/s6 build. Avoid full reparses/echo loops on selection updates; set a supported note-size/performance budget in S001 LLD.
nonFunctional.security: The home-dir scratchpad store stays outside repo enrollment per k4; the daemon's new index only joins validated target identity (sc1/sc2), never widening default document search or repo registration to the store itself. Bundle editor assets locally under CSP. Validate bridge actions, target URI and version; no arbitrary file paths, command dispatch or cloud calls from document content. Library AI features remain disabled. Native I/O follows accepted VS Code behavior; guarded store operations remain distinct.
nonFunctional.observability: Log identity/version and operation failures without note text. Surface unsupported syntax and synchronization errors while preserving original content/drafts. Distinguish fake tests from live host evidence.
nonFunctional.durability: sc1's stableId must survive rename/move/archive/restore (s7); the daemon index's reconciliation strategy against the home-dir store's actual file state (so it never serves a stale binding indefinitely) is a design.story decision. Never write/normalize merely by opening a file. Unknown syntax, custom links and diagram fences must round-trip or unsafe edits must be refused with the original preserved. Never silently overwrite newer revisions. Validate cross-window conflict, undo/redo, reload and recovery against normal VS Code behavior.

One document controller per URI per window owns canonical application. Pane owns timer/codec worker; native service owns host grammar executor. Each executor has at most one running job plus latest queued work, and cannot write files or invoke commands directly.

dataModelChanges.details: Add explicit staged/waiting-idle/validating/authorized/applied/conflict distinctions. Pending admission is not a conflict. Track latest immutable intent and exact base, keep one apply in flight, never auto-authorize newer unvalidated typing.

Existing bounded draft identity is staged with apply:false and later authorized for the same content/sequence. Durable receipt does not authorize native application. Atomically migrate all producer/parser/controller/test consumers; no permissive arbitrary-command fields.

Proposed private immutable job keyed by executor epoch, pane session, draftSeq, base version/digest and configured-codec identity, carrying bounded source references/draft and an actual-document intent fingerprint. Fingerprint semantics match the existing document comparator, including its sole heading-id exception. A parsed copy of the draft cannot serve as its own expected intent. A failed or superseded job never mutates the TextDocument.

New private executor modules are proposed, not current APIs. Keep 1 MiB text and 2 MiB ordinary message limits. Base transfer and candidate jobs use separate bounded messages; do not combine several full snapshots into an oversized message. Worker has no native file/chat/command access. Browser worker is a single local bundled script loaded from trusted fixed code via blob/data-compatible VS Code loading; document content is data only. Retain connect-src 'none', add only the required worker-src policy, terminate/revoke on disposal. Worker codec parity/CSP/native loading are an early qualification gate. Host grammar worker is extension-owned and independently verifies source admission.

Split recovery staging/pending from admission/refusal; atomically update producer, closed parser, renderer state, controller and action consumers. Add bounded executors, exact-generation identities, verified-base caching and cancellation.

alternativesConsidered.name: Idle timer on the renderer thread
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Coalesce edits until a 300 ms gap, then perform the existing full validation on the renderer thread.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Keep the existing one-pane controller and add one trailing-edge timer. Lightweight draft capture runs per transaction; timer expiry runs current fidelity admission. Explicit commands flush. This is the smallest scheduling change, but the measured full pass still blocks resumed typing and cannot honestly meet the existing render target during validation.
pros: Minimal API changes and direct reuse of the current codec/admission routines.
Eliminates repeated validation during a continuous typing burst.
cons: A multi-second main-thread pass still freezes input after the gap.
Does not solve the measured full-bound latency requirement.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Smallest code change, but fails the performance part of ac1.

alternativesConsidered.name: Idle-coalesced background admission
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Render and retain drafts immediately; validate only the latest idle generation in background execution before authorizing native application.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Reuse the existing draft/controller/recovery boundary, adding a non-conflicting pending-validation state and explicit generation-bound admission/flush. A 300 ms trailing-edge gap starts full fidelity verification outside the input thread; newer typing supersedes its result. Cache only fully verified immutable bases keyed by exact source/version/digest and codec version, and share a parse within a validation job without dropping checks. Background configured-codec validation must use the same factored schema/serializer as the live editor and pass the full corpus. Host admission remains independently verified and runs once per admitted generation. Preserve 1 MiB/2 MiB bounds, explicit native application, recovery receipts and source/session checks. Worker packaging and codec equivalence are qualification gates, not assumed existing capabilities.
pros: Separates responsiveness, recoverability and verified canonical application.
Matches idle-gap behavior while protecting resumed typing during a long pass.
Preserves all fidelity checks and existing source/sequence guards.
cons: Requires private protocol/state and worker/schema factoring changes plus native requalification.
Actual 1 MiB latency remains a measured gate; a timer alone or unverified worker equivalence is insufficient.

alternativesConsidered.name: Validation only on explicit Save
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep local editing fast and defer all validation until an explicit Save.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Retain local drafts and validate only on Save, with no idle canonical application. Keep existing source identity and UI. This removes per-keystroke validation but leaves native document synchronization and autosave dependent on an explicit action rather than the requested typing gap.
pros: Simple separation of typing from expensive checks.
cons: Does not implement the user's idle-gap requirement.
Leaves native TextDocument and autosave stale indefinitely and weakens the agreed lifecycle behavior.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Weakens ac1 and complicates ac4 despite simple local typing.
